newsitem.title: USA: Wash. state judge agrees to review Liggett papers.
newsitem.headline: Wash. state judge agrees to review Liggett papers.

text.p: A Washington state judge on Thursday said he would accept about six boxes of tobacco industry documents to determine which ones could be released to state attorneys.

King County Superior Court Judge George Finkle said in an order he would accept under seal the documents from Liggett Group Inc, which has waived its attorney-client privilege over the information as part of a settlement with Washington and 21 other states.
Liggett, a unit of Brooke Group Ltd, also agreed to pay states 25 percent of its pretax profits for the next 25 years to settle claims over the health-related costs of smoking.
Liggett's co-defendants in the Washington state suit, including the largest U.S. tobacco companies, contend Liggett cannot unilaterally waive the attorney-client privilege over many of the documents.

John Hough, an assistant Washington state attorney general, said Liggett had separated out documents that may involve other companies, but the state has asked Finkle to read the Liggett-only documents first to determine whether they could be released to the state.
Finkle has entered a protective order preventing public release of any documents in the suit to protect trade secrets.
But he said he would evaluate each document in the latest batch to determine whether the confidentiality order will continue to apply.

Judges in six other states also are considering the so-called privileged documents. A court in Mississippi has ordered the documents released to state attorneys, but tobacco companies have appealed to the state supreme court.
